findings.description: No server_side_encryption_configuration block is defined, so objects placed in this bucket (which stores reports) are stored unencrypted at rest by default.
This bucket holds ledger/financial export data but has no server_side_encryption_configuration, leaving sensitive financial data unencrypted at rest.
Versioning and access logging are configured but no server_side_encryption_configuration is present, so stored model artifacts are unencrypted at rest.
No server_side_encryption_configuration block is defined for this bucket, leaving operational runbook contents unencrypted at rest.

The acl value "lcatalogopts-delivery-write" is not a valid AWS canned ACL name; if this is meant to grant log-delivery write access it should use a scoped bucket policy rather than a broad canned ACL, and as written risks unintended access control behavior on a bucket holding audit logs.
There is no aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block associated with this bucket, so there is no explicit guardrail preventing the bucket from being made public via a future bucket policy or ACL change.
No aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block is configured for this financial data bucket, leaving no defense-in-depth control against accidental public exposure.
No aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block is configured for this audit log bucket, so a misapplied ACL or bucket policy could expose audit trail data publicly with no compensating control.
No aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block resource is attached to this bucket, providing no guardrail against future public exposure.
No aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block resource is attached to this bucket, providing no guardrail against future public exposure.
